content:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod - kv-cache.eviction_rate exceeded threshold (5m average)

maria (oncall): saw this at 09:04 PT, paging kicked in. customer impact looks limited but noisy — lots of repeated pages. digging now. :coffee:

sam (eng-sre): pinging infra — is there a deploy or config change? I don't see recent kernel/driver bumps. @kevin any infra events?

kevin (eng-sre): no infra deploys in the window. looks like eviction bursts correlate with a few heavy embedding ingest jobs starting around 09:00. I can confirm KV miss ratio spiked too.

ellie (support): got two customer tickets, both reported transient 500s while ingesting embeddings. tickets: https://zendesk.company/agent/tickets/9812, https://zendesk.company/agent/tickets/9813

maria (oncall): ok, customer impact -> intermittent errors for a small subset. mitigation: I'm enabling a temporary alert squelch to prevent pager fatigue while we triage. will annotate the alert with incident id.

sam (eng-sre): agree squelch while we investigate, but we should also fix the alert to reduce noise — current rule uses a 1m avg and fires on small bursts. propose: change to a 5m rolling avg and require >3 hosts affected.

maria (oncall): suggested alert snippet (will file PR):

```yaml
alert: HighKVCacheEvictionRate
expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_eviction_rate[5m]) > 0.12
labels:
  severity: page
for: 5m
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions
  play: "Investigate eviction spikes, check embedding jobs and ingress rates"
```

kevin (eng-sre): that looks reasonable. also add a dimension to ignore small-scale background batch workers: `by(instance, job)` and threshold only if count(instance) > 3.

sam (eng-sre): will open PR to monitoring repo: https://git.internal/redwood/monitoring/pull/472 - includes rule change + dashboard update. cc: @maria for runbook annotation content.

maria (oncall): filing a short post-incident checklist in the runbook and linking dashboard panels. runbook URL: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions. I'll add an "Alert tuning" section with timestamps and owner.

ellie (support): can you add a short note for support on how to respond to tickets while the change rolls out? e.g., check ingestion window, advise retry, collect job ids.

maria (oncall): added support note draft in the runbook and created a PR for the runbook: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/221 - includes a short FAQ and a link to the grafana panel.

incident-bot: Runbook updated by maria (oncall) — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions#alert-tuning

sam (eng-sre): dashboard change: added a heatmap of eviction_rate by host + ingestion job tags. panel link: https://grafana.company/d/evictions/kv-evictions?orgId=1

kevin (eng-sre): operational plan:
- short-term: merge monitoring rule change (5m avg + min-hosts) and deploy to staging today.
- medium-term: throttle/soft-quota ingestion jobs that cause bursts, coordinate with ML team.
- long-term: KV service improvements for backpressure.

maria (oncall): handing over to night on-call @kevin for follow-up and to watch for regressions after PR deploy.

kevin (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll watch the new rule after rollout and validate alerts remain meaningful. setting an annotation in pager duty: "monitoring rule change deployed - watch for suppressed pages".

ellie (support): will update customer tickets with the mitigation notes and link runbook/dashboard.

maria (oncall): post-incident actions (summary):
- PR opened for alert rule change: https://git.internal/redwood/monitoring/pull/472 (sam)
- Runbook annotated and support FAQ PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/221 (maria)
- Dashboard panels added: https://grafana.company/d/evictions/kv-evictions (sam)
- Owner for follow-up: kevin (overnight)

maria (oncall): marking this thread resolved for immediate paging but keeping it pinned for follow-up notes. :white_check_mark:

kevin (eng-sre): noted. will post results of the staging rollout and any threshold tweaks in this thread.

incident-bot: Incident closed (no active pages).
